PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit unacceptable-loss framing
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Military/aerospace system safety; later STPA made losses an explicit first step.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Define mishaps/accidents and unacceptable consequences before selecting hazards and controls.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Safety work can optimise compliance or component metrics without knowing what outcome must be prevented.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unacceptable injury, fatality, mission loss, environmental harm, critical-service loss or other explicitly governed loss.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Analysis and controls are aimed at proxies while the actual loss remains unarticulated or shifts unnoticed.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Name losses, affected stakeholders and decision authority; derive hazardous system states and constraints from them.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any consequential system, material change, novel operation or unresolved safety decision.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For trivial reversible work, state the bounded loss in one line and use the authoritative deterministic check; no elaborate taxonomy.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stakeholders and authority must be known; loss statements must be specific enough to discriminate decisions.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: A competent owner must be authorised to define tolerability and resolve conflicts among safety, mission and availability.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Evidence that the loss set still matches current use, users, environment and public exposure.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents safety effort from becoming method-first and exposes value conflicts early.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design authority, operator, regulator or risk-acceptance authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Losses framed too broadly become slogans; too narrowly omit public/mission harms; economic inconvenience can be mislabelled as safety.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Different domains define accident, mishap and harm differently; not every adverse outcome is a safety loss.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from accident categories to stakeholder-explicit loss models linked to hazards, constraints and acceptance authority.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A concise, current, decision-linked definition of unacceptable loss that bounds later analysis without pretending completeness.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is the decision boundary; a “loss list” document or STPA worksheet is optional.

EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH: HIGH — origin and transmission are documented in primary or authoritative historical sources.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.FORMAL_OR_MODEL_STRENGTH: MODERATE — mechanism is coherent but depends on model scope and assumptions.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.ACCIDENT_CASE_STRENGTH: MODERATE — multiple cases exhibit the mechanism, but case evidence is not a controlled estimate of effect size.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_STRENGTH: LOW_TO_MODERATE — controlled or comparative field evidence is uneven across domains.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.DOMAIN_PRACTICE_STRENGTH: HIGH — established in mature high-consequence practice when properly scoped.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.STANDARD_OR_REGULATORY_STRENGTH: HIGH — required or recognised in one or more authoritative regimes; this is practice authority, not optimality proof.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH: MODERATE_TO_HIGH — mechanism transfers when the same hazard/control conditions exist; artefacts do not automatically transfer.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY: HIGH — value depends on boundary, model, data, authority, independence and current configuration.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH: MODERATE — implementation failures and scope critiques materially constrain use.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.SOURCE_BASIS: Primary: S012, S014, S015, S018, S033; critical/contrary: S038, S066.

PROPERTIES.EMPIRICAL_OR_DOMAIN_EVIDENCE: NASA and DoD lifecycle safety frameworks; STPA loss/hazard step; ISO/IEC safety terminology.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No source establishes one universal loss vocabulary or acceptable threshold.
PROPERTIES.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should distributional, long-latency and intergenerational harms be represented without making every objective a safety loss?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Hazardous system-state framing distinct from failure
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Direct system safety and process safety; sharpened by STAMP/STPA and SOTIF.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Identify a system condition that, with a particular environment or set of conditions, can lead to loss.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Teams equate hazards with failed parts and therefore miss unsafe nominal behaviour, exposure and interaction.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: A system state or condition capable of contributing to unacceptable loss.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: No component is classified as failed, yet the system enters an unsafe state through context, interaction, performance insufficiency or exposure.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Model hazards separately from causes; then search failures, interactions, environmental conditions and control flaws that can create them.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Systems with software, humans, adaptive functions, hazardous energy/material, changing environments or nontrivial interfaces.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A simple local task with a complete deterministic invariant may use that invariant directly rather than a separate hazard ontology.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: A defined system boundary, environment and loss relation; hazards must be controllable enough to inform design or operation.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Ownership of system boundary and authority to impose constraints across components/interfaces.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Observable indicators of hazardous state, exposure and boundary conditions—not only component health.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Broadens causal coverage and separates what must be prevented from how it may arise.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System architect, safety engineer, operations authority and design teams.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Hazards become vague nouns, duplicate losses, or are listed without a consumer/control.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Hazard definitions differ across MIL-STD-882, IEC/ISO, process safety and STPA; terminology should not be forced.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from hardware-energy and failure hazards to system-state, interaction, intended-function and sociotechnical hazards.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A current loss-linked hazardous-state model with explicit boundary, exposure and causal assumptions.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is the loss-capable state model; exact hazard-log columns are not required.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Enforceable safety constraints
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: System-safety requirements and design-control traditions; explicit constraint concept in STAMP/STPA.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Translate hazards into requirements, prohibitions, limits and control obligations.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Hazards are identified but no enforceable design/operational condition prevents or limits them.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss arising because the system permits a hazardous state or action outside its safe envelope.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A “control” is documented but not allocated, implemented, verified, monitored or enforceable in operation.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Derive constraints from hazards; allocate them to controllers/components/procedures; verify implementation and operational enforcement.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Whenever a credible hazard remains after elimination or redesign.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Where a deterministic existing rule already proves the safe condition, record/reuse it rather than create duplicate safety requirements.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Constraint must be testable or otherwise assessable and tied to a controller with feasible authority.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The allocated controller must possess real control authority and resources; responsibility without authority is insufficient.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: State/feedback showing the constraint is maintained and alarms when it is violated or unverifiable.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts analysis into design/operation change and makes later assurance falsifiable.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design authority, controller owner, verifier, operator and acceptance authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Vague “shall be safe” statements, contradictory constraints, unenforceable human instructions, and unmonitored assumptions.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Constraint language can become model bureaucracy; not all safety behaviour is reducible to static rules.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from safety requirements to allocated control constraints with runtime observability, change impact and recovery semantics.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: The minimum sufficient constraint is explicit, allocated, enforceable, verified and paired with feedback or bounded assurance.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A requirements database is optional; live allocation and enforcement are the property.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Lifecycle hazard identification with explicit completeness boundaries
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Military/aerospace programme safety, process hazard analysis and medical-device lifecycle risk management.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Perform preliminary, system, subsystem, operating/support and change hazard analysis across lifecycle phases.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Hazards introduced in manufacture, operation, maintenance, disposal or changed environment are omitted from design-only analysis.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unacceptable loss from an unsearched lifecycle phase, stakeholder or operational scenario.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: The hazard population is treated as complete because a meeting or worksheet ended, despite unsearched boundaries or new evidence.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define search scope, phases, methods, expertise, exclusions, assumptions and residual unknowns; revisit on triggers.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Novel/high-consequence systems; phase transitions; operational change; significant incidents; emerging evidence.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Low-consequence reversible work needs only a bounded check of known hazards and the deterministic discriminator, not a comprehensive workshop.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Access to lifecycle knowledge and representative operators/maintainers; explicit stopping/saturation criteria.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: A named owner must decide when coverage is sufficient and when reopening is required.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Coverage ledger, unresolved assumptions, operational signals and change triggers.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces systematic blind spots and makes completeness claims auditable rather than absolute.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Safety manager, system owner, change authority and risk acceptor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Checklist completion, duplicate analyses, expertise gaps, search stopping by schedule, and stale hazard logs.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: True completeness is unprovable for open systems; exhaustive process can consume effort without changing design.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from fixed phase analyses to bounded, trigger-driven, multi-method lifecycle searches with explicit residual uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Claim bounded coverage over a declared population; never claim that all possible hazards are known.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is coverage and reopening discipline; a prescribed list of analysis reports is domain-specific.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Component failure-effects analysis as a bounded complement
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: MIL-P-1629/FMECA reliability ancestry, later generalised in IEC 60812.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Enumerate item/function failure modes and trace local and system effects, causes, detection and treatment.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Single-point or component-level failure mechanisms remain undiscovered until integration or operation.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss caused by a plausible item/function failure and its propagated effects.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A component failure has hazardous effects, is undetected, or combines with other conditions not represented in design.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Perform function/item-based FMEA/FMECA focused on safety-significant elements and feed results into system hazard/control analysis.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Hardware/component/process failure modes are material and interfaces are sufficiently defined.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Skip a full worksheet where the component is non-safety-significant, trivially replaceable, or a validated deterministic test already exhausts the relevant failure set.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined functions/boundaries, knowledgeable participants and connection to system consequences and controls.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Owners must be able to change design, detection, maintenance or architecture based on findings.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Failure detection coverage, field failures, common-cause data and control effectiveness.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Finds concrete single-point failures and supports design/maintenance decisions.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Component designer, system safety analyst, reliability engineer and verifier.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Mechanical worksheet completion, arbitrary ranking, omission of interactions/software/operational context and stale failure libraries.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Bottom-up FMEA can miss unsafe interactions without component failure and is often undermined by weak occurrence data.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from exhaustive hardware tables to function/interface-focused, risk-significant analyses combined with top-down and interaction methods.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use FMEA for what it represents well; do not treat a completed FMEA as a complete system-safety analysis.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is structured failure search and effect propagation; the worksheet and RPN are not general requirements.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Top-down causal-path and logical analysis
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fault-tree analysis from Minuteman launch-control safety; event-tree/PRA expansion in aerospace and nuclear safety.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Start from an undesired top event and decompose necessary/sufficient combinations; model consequence branches after initiators.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Critical combinations, cut sets, dependencies or escalation paths are not visible in bottom-up lists.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: A defined hazardous top event or consequence sequence.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: The top event occurs through a combination of failures/conditions that was not understood or quantitatively bounded.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Construct qualitative logic first; quantify only with defensible data/dependence models; use event trees for post-initiator progression.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A well-defined top event, architecture and causal logic; quantitative use requires data and dependence modelling.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a simple deterministic invariant, use direct proof/test; do not construct a tree that merely restates the invariant.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable boundary, meaningful decomposition and explicit common-cause/uncertainty assumptions.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Decision owner can act on dominant cut sets, barriers or design alternatives.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Configuration currentness, event definitions, dependency/common-cause evidence and operational data.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Finds combinations and dominant contributors; supports barrier design, test priorities and risk-informed decisions.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System safety/PRA analyst, architect, operations and risk authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Omitted events, false independence, boundary truncation, unjustified probabilities and treating tree completeness as world completeness.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Trees represent only modelled causes and may omit organisational/software interactions and adaptive behaviour.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved into qualitative/quantitative hybrid analysis with explicit uncertainty, common-cause models and combination with interaction methods.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use top-down logic where the event structure is meaningful; pair it with other searches for unmodelled interactions and organisational causes.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is transparent causal decomposition; gate symbols and large diagrams are optional.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Structured process-deviation search
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: ICI process safety, HAZOP development from 1963; later IEC 61882.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Apply guidewords to design intent and process parameters in a multidisciplinary review to find deviations, causes, consequences and safeguards.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Credible hazardous deviations and operability problems are missed because reviewers follow normal-flow narratives.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from process deviation, abnormal operation or interaction between process parameters and safeguards.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A deviation arises outside assumed intent or a safeguard is inadequate/dependent.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use guidewords or equivalent structured prompts at nodes/functions; record decisions, actions and unresolved assumptions.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Hazardous processes, complex flows/procedures or modifications where deviation search has decision value.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not convene a full HAZOP for a tiny reversible change with a complete change discriminator; use focused review.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Accurate design intent, competent multidisciplinary team, bounded nodes and action follow-through.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Facilitator/review team must be able to obtain design changes or escalate unresolved hazards.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Action completion, safeguard state, deviations/near misses and change currentness.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Systematically challenges normal-operation assumptions and finds process/interface deviations.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Process design authority, operations, maintenance and hazard owner.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Guideword ritual, excessive scope, fatigue, repeated low-value findings and action lists without closure.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Conventional HAZOP does not by itself estimate likelihood or establish complete causal coverage.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved into proportionate, procedure/software/change HAZOP variants integrated with barrier and risk analysis.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Structured deviation prompts plus empowered expertise and action closure; method depth proportional to hazard and change.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is disciplined deviation search; exact guideword tables and workshop duration are not universal.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Unsafe interaction and unsafe-control analysis
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: General system-safety interaction reasoning; control-theoretic reformulation in STAMP/STPA; convergent evidence in SOTIF and accident analysis.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Search for system-level hazardous interactions and control actions that are missing, provided, mistimed, misordered, too long or too short.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Locally correct or nonfailed components, software, humans and organisations compose into a hazardous state.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss arising from unsafe coordination/control rather than a single failed component.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: An action is unsafe in context, missing when required, delivered at the wrong time/order/duration, or combined with conflicting actions.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Model controllers, controlled processes, actions, context and feedback; identify unsafe combinations and causal scenarios.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Software-intensive, autonomous, tightly coupled, multi-controller or human-automation systems.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Where a simple component failure fully determines the hazard, use the cheaper failure analysis and direct control; do not force a control diagram.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: A usable control/interaction model, representative operational knowledge and explicit system boundary.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Controllers must have clear authority and conflict-resolution rules; analysis findings need a design/operations consumer.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Actual action timing/order/duration, process state, controller modes, feedback quality and handoffs.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Finds hazard classes that component reliability and failure lists systematically underrepresent.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System architect, software/control designer, human factors, operations and safety authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Subjective models, analyst-dependent results, diagram growth, unvalidated completeness and failure to connect scenarios to controls.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: STPA is not uniquely entitled to interaction reasoning; other system safety, SOTIF, HAZOP and scenario methods can contribute.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward hybrid analyses that combine failure, interaction, scenario and formal verification around the actual hazard class.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Explicitly reason about unsafe composition and control context, using the cheapest adequate representation and complementary techniques.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is interaction/control reasoning; STPA terminology and diagrams are optional.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Closed-loop control and feedback integrity
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Control engineering imported into system safety; explicit in STAMP/STPA and protection-system practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Treat safety as maintaining constraints through controllers, actions, controlled processes and feedback.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A command is assumed to equal achieved state, or feedback is absent, stale, wrong or semantically insufficient.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss because the controlled process did not reach or remain in the intended safe state.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: The controller issues a nominally safe command but actuation fails, process response differs, or feedback falsely confirms success.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Specify required state feedback, freshness, validity and independent confirmation; design fallback for unobservable state.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Consequential control actions, remote/autonomous actuation, interlocks, shutdown, recovery and distributed control.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For local directly observable reversible actions, immediate observation/test can serve as the feedback path without additional instrumentation.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Sensor/feedback path coverage, semantics and timing must match the safety decision.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Controller must be authorised to act on missing/invalid feedback and to enter a safe/degraded mode.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: State-based confirmation, feedback freshness/integrity, actuator/process health and observability gaps.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents command-success, API-success or paperwork-success from being mistaken for physical safety.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Controller, operator, safety monitor and restart authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Common-mode sensor errors, feedback derived from the command rather than process, alarm flooding and unhandled uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Additional sensors can share failure modes; feedback can create complexity or false confidence.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from simple interlocks to integrity-monitored, time-aware feedback with explicit unobservable/degraded-state behaviour.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every consequential control has evidence sufficient to establish intended state, or the system treats state as unknown and constrains operation.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is state confirmation and bounded response; a particular control diagram is not required.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Controller process-model and mode consistency
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Human factors mode-awareness work and STAMP/STPA process-model concept.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Ensure the controller’s model of process state, mode, environment and control authority matches reality sufficiently for safe action.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Operator, automation or organisation acts rationally on a stale, incomplete or wrong model.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from mode confusion, automation surprise, incorrect state inference or hidden environmental change.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A command is safe in the believed state but unsafe in the actual state.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Expose modes and assumptions; reconcile state estimates; detect divergence; design transitions and fallback behaviour.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Mode-rich automation, distributed systems, remote operation, delayed observability or adaptive functions.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A stateless local action with directly visible conditions may require only a simple precondition check.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Model variables must be linked to observable state and updated at a rate adequate to the hazard dynamics.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Controller must be able to refuse action or escalate when model confidence is insufficient.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Current mode/state, transition completion, environment, authority and model-confidence indicators.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces contextually unsafe commands and human-automation coordination failures.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Automation designer, interface/human-factors engineer, operator and controller owner.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Hidden modes, inconsistent displays, stale caches, unverifiable AI state and overloading operators with mode detail.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Perfect model agreement is impossible; excessive transparency can increase workload.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward explicit state/mode contracts, confidence/uncertainty handling and transition verification.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Make safety-relevant process-model assumptions visible, monitored and fail-bounded.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is model-state consistency; a STPA “process model” box is optional.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Timing, ordering, duration and transition semantics
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Real-time control/system safety; explicit unsafe-control-action classes in STPA.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Analyse not only whether an action occurs but when, in what order, for how long and during which transition.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Correct commands become unsafe because of latency, reordering, repetition, premature stop or excessive duration.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss during transient states or because control timing violates the safe envelope.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Action sequencing and state transitions compose into a hazardous condition despite correct static requirements.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Specify temporal constraints, transition guards, timeouts, idempotence/repetition bounds and completion feedback.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Real-time, distributed, asynchronous, autonomous, start-up/shutdown and handoff operations.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A synchronous local operation with atomic deterministic semantics may need only a direct timeout/completion check.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known timing budgets, transition states, clock/order assumptions and failure handling.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Controller/arbitrator can enforce ordering and block unsafe transitions.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Timestamped actions, transition state, completion, retries, timeout and causal order.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Finds hazards invisible to static pass/fail requirements.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Control/software architect, operator and verifier.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Unrealistic timing models, unsynchronised clocks, hidden queues and excessive temporal-state complexity.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Temporal formalisation can be expensive and false precision can hide uncertain physical timing.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved into explicit transition-state assurance, runtime monitors and targeted temporal formal methods.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Apply temporal rigour where timing can change safety; use direct atomic checks where it cannot.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is temporal safety semantics; sequence diagrams or temporal logic are optional implementations.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Interface assumptions and safety contracts
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Systems engineering/interface control, aerospace system safety and software assurance; repeatedly exposed by accidents.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Record what each subsystem/controller assumes and guarantees at interfaces, including units, ranges, modes, timing, environment and failure semantics.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Components satisfy local requirements while incompatible assumptions create a system hazard.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from interface mismatch, hidden dependency, incompatible reuse or supplier boundary.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: An assumption changes or was never true, but downstream evidence remains apparently valid.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Make safety-relevant assumptions explicit, owned, testable and change-linked; validate at integration and operation.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Reuse, supplier integration, distributed control, configuration change, multiple organisations or novel environment.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A local isolated component with no safety-relevant interface can use a direct type/range check.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable interface identity, access to supplier evidence and ability to test cross-boundary behaviour.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: An integrator must own end-to-end safety; suppliers need change-notification obligations.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Interface conformance, assumption validity, integration state, version and environment.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents “all parts passed” from substituting for safe composition.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System integrator, supplier manager, architect and change authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Document-only contracts, untestable assumptions, version drift and organisational gaps in authority.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Formal contracts can omit human/physical context and create false completeness.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from interface control documents to executable contracts, integration tests and live assumption monitors.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Safety-relevant assumptions are explicit, version-bound, validated and invalidated by change.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is managed assumption/guarantee integrity; a particular ICD format is not required.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Common-cause, common-mode and dependent-failure reasoning
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Reliability/PRA and defence-in-depth; strengthened by software-diversity experiments and accident evidence.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Analyse dependencies that can defeat multiple channels, barriers, versions or evidence sources at once.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Nominal redundancy is treated as independent even though channels share requirements, sensors, environment, tools, power, people or assumptions.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss after multiple supposedly protective elements fail or misbehave together.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A shared cause or dependency invalidates multiplication of individual reliabilities or barrier-count confidence.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Map shared resources/assumptions and environmental causes; diversify where effective; monitor isolation and test common-cause scenarios.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Redundant/high-integrity architectures, multi-version software, layered barriers and independent evidence claims.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No detailed common-cause model is needed when there is only one simple reversible control and failure is directly detectable.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Architecture/dependency visibility and data or justified bounds for quantitative claims.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: System authority can change architecture and reject nominal independence claims.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Shared-resource health, coincident failures, barrier independence, environment and evidence lineage.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents redundancy and evidence count from overstating risk reduction.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, PRA/reliability analyst, assurance authority and operator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Unknown dependencies, poorly justified beta factors, added complexity and diversity that is only cosmetic.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Diversity can add faults and maintenance burden; common-cause probabilities are often data-poor.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from hardware common-cause models to shared-requirement/tool/data/organisation and informational-dependence analysis.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Claim independence only after identifying shared causes and monitoring the assumptions that sustain it.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is dependence-aware reasoning; a specific common-cause worksheet is not required.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Redundancy with demonstrated independence, diversity and observability
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Reliability engineering, fault tolerance, defence-in-depth and high-reliability operations.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Add alternate paths/channels/barriers so one failure does not cause loss.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Single-point failure or unavailable function causes catastrophic loss.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from failure of a critical function or barrier with no effective alternative.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Redundant channels share a cause, disagree without resolution, mask latent failure or increase complexity beyond operational control.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use redundancy only with justified independence/diversity, disagreement handling, health monitoring, maintenance and safe voting/arbitration.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-consequence single-point failures where alternate means are feasible and do not create greater interaction risk.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not add redundancy to low-consequence reversible functions when a simpler reliable design and direct detection is safer.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Independent failure modes, bounded interaction complexity, monitoring and maintainability.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Architecture owner must control shared resources and resolve channel disagreement.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Channel health, disagreement, latent failures, common resources and degraded capability.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces single-failure vulnerability when independence assumptions hold.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System architect, operator and maintenance authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Common-mode failures, mode confusion, latent standby failure, voter failure, maintenance error and workaround complexity.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: More redundancy is not monotonically safer; software diversity experiments reject naive independence.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from channel count to monitored, dependency-aware and mission-contextual fault tolerance.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the simplest architecture that meets the loss constraint, with explicit dependence and degraded-mode semantics.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is effective alternate control; a fixed number of channels is not general.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Scenario and causal-path coverage through complementary methods
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Convergence of system hazard analyses, FTA/ETA, HAZOP, PRA, scenario analysis and STPA.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Use multiple representations to search different causal classes and reconcile their findings.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A single method’s blind spots are mistaken for absence of hazards.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss through a failure, interaction, environmental, organisational or recovery path outside the selected technique’s representation.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Method scope determines what can be found, but scope is implicit or unchallenged.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Choose methods by hazard class; cross-check top-down, bottom-up, deviation, interaction and operational scenarios; stop when marginal decision value is low.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Complex/high-consequence systems with heterogeneous causal mechanisms or deep uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use one cheap deterministic analysis when it exhausts the relevant causal question; do not stack methods for prestige.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit method assumptions, shared system model, reconciliation of conflicting results and action consumers.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Safety lead can tailor methods and reject duplicative analysis.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Coverage by causal class, unresolved contradictions, new evidence and decision changes attributable to each method.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Improves hazard discovery while exposing model dependence and duplication.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Safety programme lead, architect and acceptance authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Method accumulation, duplicated artefacts from the same assumptions, inconsistent boundaries and no decision impact.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Comparative method studies are limited; “more methods” can consume experts and dilute attention.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from prescribed task lists to objectives-driven, risk-informed portfolios with explicit coverage and stop rules.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the smallest complementary portfolio that covers the credible causal classes and changes a live decision.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is representation coverage; named-method maximalism is ceremony.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Human–automation coordination and mode awareness
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Human factors, aviation automation research, medical usability and systems safety.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Design allocation, displays, modes, handoffs and fallback so humans and automation maintain a shared actionable model.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Automation and human each behave locally as designed while coordination, attention or authority fails.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from mode confusion, automation surprise, out-of-the-loop performance, workload or ambiguous handoff.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Control transfers without comprehension, warning or adequate time; automation masks or creates unsafe state.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Analyse joint cognitive work, critical tasks, mode/state visibility, workload, takeover time and fallback authority.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Automated/highly interactive systems, degraded modes and safety-critical handoffs.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a transparent local tool with direct reversible effect, use simple status/confirmation rather than a full human-factors programme.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Representative users, realistic scenarios and authority to change automation/interface design.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Clear authority for takeover, inhibit, escalation and refusal; operator responsibility must match information/control.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Mode/state, automation intent, limits, alert salience, workload and handoff completion.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces coordination failures and avoids treating the operator as a universal safety net.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Human-factors engineer, automation designer, operator authority and safety assessor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Training used to compensate for poor design, alarm overload, impossible takeover expectations and blame after loss.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Human performance is variable; interface validation in tests may not cover rare operational combinations.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from operator-error control to joint-system design, local-rationality analysis and validated critical-task performance.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Allocate work and authority around realistic human/automation capabilities, with observable modes and verified handoffs.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is coordinated control; a generic “human in the loop” claim is not evidence.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Authority, responsibility, stop and handoff clarity
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: System-safety programme management, high-reliability operations, accident investigation and control theory.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Assign who may act, stop, inhibit, accept risk, escalate, restart and resolve conflicts.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Responsibility is assigned without real authority, or overlapping authorities create gaps/conflict at the critical moment.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss because no actor can or will enforce the safety constraint or because handoff leaves a control gap.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Unsafe action proceeds under schedule pressure, ambiguous ownership or ineffective escalation.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define decision rights, stop authority, escalation, handoff state and independent acceptance for consequential exceptions.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Multi-team, supplier, regulator, autonomous/human and emergency operations; any high-consequence exception.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A single-person low-consequence local task needs only clear ownership and undo capability.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Competence, accessible information, non-retaliatory escalation and feasible control options.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Authority must be real, resourced and insulated enough to counter production pressure; acceptance authority must be named.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Open decisions, escalations, handoff acknowledgement, stop response and unresolved hazards.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents governance voids and makes accountability correspond to controllability.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System owner, operators, safety authority, management and regulator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Nominal stop authority without protection, committee diffusion, approval bottlenecks and responsibility dumping.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Rigid authority can suppress local adaptation; independence can slow feedback and fragment ownership.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward explicit control-authority maps, protected reporting, dynamic handoffs and consequence-based independence.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every consequential constraint has an actor with information, competence and authority to enforce it; handoffs transfer state as well as responsibility.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is effective authority; titles, boards and RACI charts are optional artefacts.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Traceability from hazards and constraints to implementation and verification
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: System safety, development assurance, functional safety and safety-case practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Connect each safety-significant hazard/constraint to design implementation, verification, operational control and evidence.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Safety requirements exist but are unimplemented, unverified, tested against the wrong configuration or orphaned after change.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss because a necessary constraint is absent or its implementation/evidence does not match the claim.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Documentation indicates compliance while the actual control path is incomplete.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Maintain bidirectional, configuration-bound links and test whether every claim has a control and every control has a hazard rationale.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Consequential controls, regulated development and systems with many suppliers/changes.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a tiny local deterministic change, one direct link from hazard/invariant to test result may be sufficient.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable identifiers, configuration management and semantic—not merely hyperlink—traceability.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Owners must be able to resolve orphaned requirements/evidence and block release where links fail.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Current configuration, verification result, unresolved links, waivers and operational monitoring.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Exposes missing implementation, stale evidence and unnecessary controls.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design authority, verifier, assurance case owner and change authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Trace-link volume without semantic review, auto-generated false completeness and unmaintainable matrices.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Traceability is not proof; linked requirements can all be wrong or derived from one flawed assumption.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward model/tool-supported impact analysis, evidence provenance and live orphan detection.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Maintain only decision-relevant traceability sufficient to show current hazard-to-control-to-evidence closure.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is semantic current linkage; a traceability matrix format is not required.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Uncertainty-aware risk representation rather than score-only governance
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: PRA/risk-analysis traditions and later explicit uncertainty critiques.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Represent consequences, frequencies/probabilities, uncertainty, assumptions, dependence and knowledge strength.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: An ordinal score or point estimate is treated as objective risk and drives acceptance/allocation without showing uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss because uncertain catastrophic risk was underestimated, misranked or threshold-gamed.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Sparse data, dependence, model error and category choices produce false precision or ranking inversion.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use scores only as transparent prompts; retain consequence and uncertainty separately; quantify where data/model warrant and sensitivity-test decisions.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Risk comparisons, prioritisation and residual-risk decisions where uncertainty can change action.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If a deterministic constraint settles the decision, do not estimate probability merely to fill a matrix.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined decision, data provenance, calibrated model and authority capable of reasoning under uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Risk authority must be able to reject unsupported precision and choose precaution/learning/monitoring.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Data quality, model sensitivity, uncertainty bounds, near misses and assumption validity.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Improves discrimination and prevents low-quality arithmetic from substituting for judgement.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Risk acceptor, designer, regulator and resource allocator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Opaque expert judgement, incomparable ordinal arithmetic, threshold gaming and expensive quantification with no decision effect.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Quantitative models can also mislead; deep uncertainty may resist probability assignment.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from matrix scores and point estimates toward plural representations, uncertainty analysis and consequence constraints.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Choose the least elaborate representation that preserves decision-relevant consequence and uncertainty; never call the score the risk.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is explicit uncertainty and decision linkage; coloured matrices are optional and often harmful.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Consequence, reversibility, coupling and observability proportionality
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Risk-informed system safety, ALARP/SFAIRP, safety-integrity/development-assurance grading and tailored regulatory practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Grade rigour, independence, containment, evidence and authority according to credible consequence and the difficulty of detecting/reversing loss.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Uniform maximal process wastes effort on trivial changes, while weak controls are applied to irreversible tightly coupled hazards.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Either under-control of high-consequence work or over-control that creates delay, workaround and service loss.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Process depth follows labels or bureaucracy rather than actual propagation, reversibility and knowledge conditions.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Assess consequence, reversibility, coupling, observability latency, recovery difficulty and uncertainty; select control strength and cheap path accordingly.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: All work, with greatest value where harm is severe, irreversible, coupled, latent or hard to test.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Local, cheap, reversible, immediately observable work with an authoritative discriminator uses a minimal check and normal engineering review.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Credible consequence model, change classification and authority to tailor both upward and downward.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: A competent risk/safety owner must be able to demand more or less control and document the basis.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Actual propagation/recovery performance, false-stop cost, near misses and whether controls change decisions.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Concentrates scarce safety effort where it has expected decision value and preserves speed where risk is bounded.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Safety/risk authority, programme leadership and operations.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Risk-class gaming, simplistic matrices, certification-category lock-in and underestimating systemic coupling.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Proportionality is not permission to ignore uncertain catastrophic hazards; ALARP interpretation is contested.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from fixed process classes to multidimensional, change-aware tailoring with explicit cheap paths and escalation triggers.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Control strength rises with credible loss and irreversibility/coupling/latency, while deterministic low-risk work remains cheap.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is justified tailoring; classification boards and matrices are implementations, not ends.

EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH: HIGH — origin and transmission are documented in primary or authoritative historical sources.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.FORMAL_OR_MODEL_STRENGTH: HIGH_FOR_LIMITS_MODERATE_FOR_ESTIMATES — mathematical critiques are strong; quantitative estimates remain data/model sensitive.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.ACCIDENT_CASE_STRENGTH: MODERATE — multiple cases exhibit the mechanism, but case evidence is not a controlled estimate of effect size.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_STRENGTH: LOW_TO_MODERATE — decision-quality comparisons are limited and domain dependent.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.DOMAIN_PRACTICE_STRENGTH: HIGH — established in mature high-consequence practice when properly scoped.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.STANDARD_OR_REGULATORY_STRENGTH: HIGH — required or recognised in one or more authoritative regimes; this is practice authority, not optimality proof.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH: MODERATE_TO_HIGH — mechanism transfers when the same hazard/control conditions exist; artefacts do not automatically transfer.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY: HIGH — value depends on boundary, model, data, authority, independence and current configuration.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH: MODERATE — implementation failures and scope critiques materially constrain use.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.SOURCE_BASIS: Primary: S014, S029, S035, S052, S053, S095, S104; critical/contrary: S036, S038, S113.

PROPERTIES.EMPIRICAL_OR_DOMAIN_EVIDENCE: FAA expressly avoids imposing structured techniques where traditional methods suffice; HSE and NRC use targeted/significance-based regulation.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No universal scalar combines consequence, reversibility, coupling and observability without information loss.
PROPERTIES.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should proportionality account for low-probability public harms when evidence is sparse and false stops are also dangerous?

CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: One direct authoritative check for local reversible work; escalate only on failed assumptions or widened consequence
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.OVER_CONTROL_FAILURE: Maximal controls can cause unavailable safety-critical service, delay, alarm fatigue and procedural bypass

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit residual-risk acceptance by competent authority
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Military system-safety risk-acceptance practice, medical-device risk management, safety cases and ALARP governance.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: After feasible controls, document the remaining hazard, assumptions and evidence and obtain acceptance at an authority level commensurate with consequence.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Residual risk disappears into an analyst score, is implicitly accepted by delivery pressure, or is approved by someone without mandate or knowledge.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unacceptable loss from a known but incompletely controlled hazard whose ownership and acceptance basis are obscure.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Risk is silently transferred, severity or uncertainty is downplayed, or acceptance persists after its assumptions expire.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: State the residual hazard and uncertainty, identify the exposed parties and control status, obtain time/configuration-bounded acceptance and reopen on change or evidence.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Consequential residual hazards that cannot presently be eliminated or further reduced at proportionate cost.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No separate acceptance ritual is needed when an authoritative deterministic check proves the hazard absent or a trivial reversible effect remains within ordinary authority.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current hazard/control evidence, explicit alternatives and uncertainty, identified exposure and a defined acceptance policy.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The acceptor must have legal/organisational mandate, relevant competence and authority over resources or operational restrictions.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Barrier health, exposure, assumptions, incidents, time/configuration limits and effectiveness of compensating controls.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents accidental or hidden risk transfer and makes the consequential tradeoff challengeable and revisable.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design authority, operator, regulator, accountable executive and affected operational owner.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Rubber-stamp boards, risk laundering through matrices, acceptance by authority remote from consequences and indefinite waivers.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Formal acceptance cannot make an intolerable risk acceptable and may exclude affected publics or workers from the decision.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward explicit residual-risk statements, bounded delegated authority, expiry conditions and operational monitoring.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A current, named and revisable decision by a competent authority over a residual hazard whose controls, uncertainty, exposure and alternatives are visible.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A signed form is not the property; accountable and evidence-bounded acceptance is.

CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.CONSEQUENCE_DIMENSION: Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.REVERSIBILITY_DIMENSION: More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.COUPLING_DIMENSION: Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment.

RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.RISK_REPRESENTATION: Named residual hazards, consequence, uncertainty, exposure, control status, assumptions and validity period.
RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.WHAT_IT_CAN_JUSTIFY: A bounded decision to operate, test, defer or add controls under explicit authority.
RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.WHAT_IT_CANNOT_JUSTIFY: Erasing moral/legal duties, accepting an unknown hazard, or converting weak evidence into safety.
RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.UNCERTAINTY_BOUNDARY: Unknown mechanisms, sparse data and changing exposure remain visible and can trigger precaution or monitoring.
RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.DATA_REQUIREMENTS: Current hazard/control evidence, practicable alternatives, exposed populations and change-sensitive assumptions.
RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.GAMING_RISK: Likelihood downgrading, fragmented hazards, acceptance at too-low authority and indefinite waivers.
RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Ordinary delegated decision when consequence is trivial, reversible and deterministically bounded.
RISK_REPRESENTATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Competent, explicit, time/configuration-bounded residual-risk acceptance with reopening triggers.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Proportionate risk reduction under ALARP or SFAIRP reasoning
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: UK health-and-safety law and regulatory decision practice, with analogous practicability and proportionality reasoning elsewhere.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Reduce risk so far as reasonably practicable rather than stop at a numerical threshold or demand literal zero risk.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Either cheap meaningful controls are omitted because a score is below threshold, or disproportionate burdens are imposed without material safety gain.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Preventable serious harm, or secondary harm and mission loss caused by indiscriminate over-control.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Cost, sacrifice, benefit and uncertainty are compared opaquely; gross disproportionality is treated as a formula; good practice becomes stale.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Identify feasible controls, establish good practice, examine remaining risk and sacrifice transparently, and require stronger justification as consequence rises.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Material occupational/process/public hazards where feasible alternatives and control costs matter.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Where a binding deterministic rule or clearly trivial reversible hazard settles the decision, use it directly rather than manufacture a cost-benefit case.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Legally appropriate jurisdiction, credible consequence evidence, feasible options and competent judgement.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The duty holder retains the burden to show sufficient reduction; a calculator or consultant cannot own the legal judgement.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Control effectiveness, changing good practice, exposure, sacrifice estimates and evidence that adopted controls remain operative.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Forces search beyond threshold compliance while retaining proportionality and practical feasibility.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Duty holder, regulator, workforce/public representative and design/operations authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Back-calculated numbers, monetisation controversy, threshold gaming and invoking cost before identifying controls.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: ALARP is jurisdiction-specific, ethically contested and frequently misunderstood; it is not a universal optimisation formula.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward transparent option analysis, good-practice presumptions, explicit uncertainty and higher burdens for catastrophic exposure.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use proportionality as disciplined justification for control sufficiency, not as a numerical escape hatch or universal legal export.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The transferable property is reasoned proportionality; the exact legal test and paperwork are domain-specific.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Defence in depth with barrier independence and degradation monitoring
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Nuclear safety and process protection, converging with layered aerospace and functional-safety architectures.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Provide multiple preventive, control, mitigation and emergency layers so one error or failure does not directly produce catastrophic loss.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A single protection, assumption or operator response is treated as sufficient for a high-consequence hazard.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Catastrophic release, loss of critical function or public harm after one failed or bypassed layer.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Layers share power, sensors, software, maintenance, environment or organisational assumptions, or degrade unnoticed.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Allocate distinct barrier purposes, analyse common cause and dependencies, monitor availability and preserve escalation/mitigation when prevention fails.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Severe, irreversible hazards for which no single control can be shown sufficiently dependable.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not add nominal layers to a trivial reversible task or where one simple physically enforced elimination removes the hazard.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Barrier functions and dependencies are explicit; surveillance and maintenance can detect degradation; emergency arrangements exist.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Owners must be able to maintain, test, isolate and restore layers and to restrict operation when defence is impaired.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Barrier demand and success, independence, common utilities, bypass status, test coverage and degraded configurations.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Limits cliff-edge failure and supplies time and alternatives for detection, containment and recovery.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, operations, maintenance, emergency management and regulator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Layer counting, shared common modes, hidden coupling, added complexity and compensatory complacency.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Fukushima and multiversion evidence show that apparent multiplicity does not establish effective independence.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from redundant layer count toward functional diversity, independence claims, degradation monitoring and severe-accident mitigation.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A hazard-specific barrier architecture whose layers have distinct functions, credible independence and live health evidence.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A bow-tie or layer diagram is optional; demonstrably effective, independent and monitored barriers are the property.

SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Defence in depth with barrier independence and degradation monitoring
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Catastrophic release, loss of critical function or public harm after one failed or bypassed layer.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROLLER: The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROLLED_PROCESS: The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.SAFETY_CONSTRAINT: The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Defence in depth with barrier independence and degradation monitoring.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROL_ACTION: Allocate distinct barrier purposes, analyse common cause and dependencies, monitor availability and preserve escalation/mitigation when prevention fails.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK: Barrier demand and success, independence, common utilities, bypass status, test coverage and degraded configurations.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.PROCESS_MODEL_ASSUMPTION: Barrier functions and dependencies are explicit; surveillance and maintenance can detect degradation; emergency arrangements exist.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.DELAY_OR_OBSERVABILITY_RISK: Delay, missing data or stale configuration can leave the controller acting on an obsolete model.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY: Owners must be able to maintain, test, isolate and restore layers and to restrict operation when defence is impaired.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Excessive analysis or intervention can delay low-consequence reversible work and induce bypass.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Do not add nominal layers to a trivial reversible task or where one simple physically enforced elimination removes the hazard.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A hazard-specific barrier architecture whose layers have distinct functions, credible independence and live health evidence.

CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Defence in depth with barrier independence and degradation monitoring
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.CONSEQUENCE_DIMENSION: Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.REVERSIBILITY_DIMENSION: More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.COUPLING_DIMENSION: Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.OBSERVABILITY_LATENCY: Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Safety-integrity and development-assurance rigour tied to safety functions
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: IEC 61508 safety integrity levels and aviation/automotive development-assurance classifications.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Classify safety functions or failure conditions and attach graded architectural, development and verification rigour.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: An assurance level is treated as a direct probability that the whole system is safe, or assigned without a valid hazard-to-function allocation.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss because a critical safety function lacks commensurate integrity, or because a process label masks unsafe interactions outside its scope.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Misallocation, systematic defects, independence assumptions, “SIL washing” and conflating process compliance with achieved reliability.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Derive integrity/assurance needs from hazards and functions; meet domain architecture and process objectives; verify actual function and complement with interaction analysis.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Safety-related E/E/PE, airborne software/hardware and automotive functions whose failure conditions justify graded assurance.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not assign a high assurance level to low-consequence code or use the classification where a direct deterministic test fully settles a local reversible change.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Valid hazard classification, allocated safety function, domain applicability and evidence that architecture and verification objectives are met.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Certification/design authorities must control classification and independence; suppliers must disclose relevant development evidence.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Function demand/success, diagnostic coverage, systematic-defect controls, requirement/verification coverage and configuration identity.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Concentrates disciplined architecture and verification on functions whose loss could be consequential.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System safety assessor, functional-safety manager, certification authority and integrator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Level inflation, lowest-bid evidence production, rote objective completion and scope gaps such as intended-function hazards.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Standards authority is strong but comparative evidence for exact level/process prescriptions is limited; SOTIF exists because malfunction-only scope is incomplete.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward explicit scope boundaries, complementary intended-function/security analyses and assurance claims about functions rather than the whole system.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use graded integrity objectives as one hazard-derived assurance mechanism, never as a numerical certificate of total system safety.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The general property is consequence-linked rigour; SIL, ASIL and DAL taxonomies are domain artefacts.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Informational independence and diversity of assurance evidence
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Independent verification/validation, diverse design and assurance-case confidence traditions.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Seek evidence generated by mechanisms, people, data and assumptions sufficiently independent to expose common blind spots.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Many reviews or artefacts derived from one requirement/model/test oracle are counted as independent confirmation.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unsafe acceptance caused by correlated evidence error, common specification defects or organisational confirmation bias.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Nominally separate teams share sources, tools, incentives, training, data or process models and reproduce the same mistake.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Map evidence provenance and dependence; combine analytic, test, operational and independent challenge where each can fail differently.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-consequence claims whose error cannot be cheaply discovered after deployment.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: One direct authoritative discriminator suffices when it conclusively decides a local reversible claim; reviewer multiplication adds no information.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence methods have explicit failure modes and provenance; independent assessors have access, competence and challenge authority.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The independent function needs organisational freedom and information access, but informational independence must be assessed separately.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Disagreements, common inputs, oracle diversity, defect yield, challenge closure and configuration coverage.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces common blind spots and provides stronger grounds for confidence than evidence count.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Safety case owner, IV&V, certification authority and risk acceptor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Independence theatre, duplicated tests, shared flawed specifications, costly segregation and delayed feedback.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Experimental multiversion evidence directly undermines naive independence assumptions; independence can also impede fast integrated learning.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from organisational separation alone toward evidence-dependence graphs, diverse failure mechanisms and risk-based independence.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Require independently informative evidence in proportion to consequence and explicitly disclose shared assumptions and sources.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A separate reviewer or document is not automatically independent evidence.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Nuclear and defence safety cases, later structured assurance cases and Goal Structuring Notation.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Make safety claims, reasoning, evidence, assumptions and context explicit enough for challenge and acceptance.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Evidence accumulates without showing what it establishes, or claims are accepted because a document appears complete.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unjustified operation or certification when the argument omits a hazard, rests on false premises or cites stale evidence.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Circular reasoning, unsupported inference, hidden context, confirmation bias and argument completion after design decisions.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Construct the minimum argument needed for live decisions; expose premises, evidence relevance, uncertainty and unresolved challenges; bind it to current configuration.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Consequential safety decisions requiring synthesis across heterogeneous evidence and organisations.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A direct deterministic proof/test and a brief recorded rationale may be the whole case for a narrow reversible claim.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined claims and consumers, trustworthy evidence, current system boundary and willingness to record uncertainty/defeaters.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The case owner must not control all challenge; acceptance authority needs power to reject or demand evidence.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Evidence validity, claim coverage, assumptions, challenge status, operational indicators and configuration/change events.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Exposes reasoning gaps, supports accountable acceptance and preserves why evidence was considered sufficient.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design authority, operator, regulator/certifier and residual-risk acceptor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Argument theatre, template completion, rhetorical overclaim, stale evidence and safety case detached from engineering work.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Nimrod is powerful counterevidence to equating a voluminous accepted case with safety; formal coherence cannot establish premise truth.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward modular, challenge-driven, confidence-aware and living cases integrated with hazard and configuration state.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A current, defeasible decision argument connecting consequential claims to relevant evidence, assumptions, uncertainty and authority.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: GSN and a monolithic document are optional notations; explicit justified reasoning is the property.
