SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unjustified operation or certification when the argument omits a hazard, rests on false premises or cites stale evidence.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROLLER: The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROLLED_PROCESS: The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.SAFETY_CONSTRAINT: The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROL_ACTION: Construct the minimum argument needed for live decisions; expose premises, evidence relevance, uncertainty and unresolved challenges; bind it to current configuration.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK: Evidence validity, claim coverage, assumptions, challenge status, operational indicators and configuration/change events.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.PROCESS_MODEL_ASSUMPTION: Defined claims and consumers, trustworthy evidence, current system boundary and willingness to record uncertainty/defeaters.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.DELAY_OR_OBSERVABILITY_RISK: Delay, missing data or stale configuration can leave the controller acting on an obsolete model.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY: The case owner must not control all challenge; acceptance authority needs power to reject or demand evidence.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Excessive analysis or intervention can delay low-consequence reversible work and induce bypass.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: A direct deterministic proof/test and a brief recorded rationale may be the whole case for a narrow reversible claim.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A current, defeasible decision argument connecting consequential claims to relevant evidence, assumptions, uncertainty and authority.

CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Claim–argument–evidence safety assurance
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.CONSEQUENCE_DIMENSION: Control depth increases with credible harm to people, mission, environment, critical service or public exposure.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.REVERSIBILITY_DIMENSION: More assurance is warranted where effects cannot be cheaply rolled back or compensated.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.COUPLING_DIMENSION: Tighter coupling and broader propagation increase the value of explicit modelling and containment.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.OBSERVABILITY_LATENCY: Longer delay between unsafe action and observable consequence increases anticipatory analysis needs.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.RECOVERY_DIFFICULTY: Difficult or ethically impossible recovery/testing increases dependence on analytical and independent evidence.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.CONTROL_STRENGTH_RELATION: Scale analysis, independence, evidence and recovery controls to consequence and uncertainty, not to labels.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: A direct deterministic proof/test and a brief recorded rationale may be the whole case for a narrow reversible claim.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.OVER_CONTROL_FAILURE: Uniform maximal treatment wastes scarce safety attention and can provoke workarounds or unavailable service.
CONSEQUENCE_REVERSIBILITY_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A current, defeasible decision argument connecting consequential claims to relevant evidence, assumptions, uncertainty and authority.

SAFETY_ASSURANCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: A bounded safety proposition needed for a live decision.

SAFETY_ASSURANCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CONTEXT: System boundary, configuration, environment, validity period and delegated authorities.
SAFETY_ASSURANCE_PROFILE.DEFEATERS_OR_CHALLENGES: Counterexamples, missing scenarios, invalid tools/data, dependence, uncertainty and operational anomalies.
SAFETY_ASSURANCE_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_REQUIREMENT: Challenge and evidence diversity scale with consequence.
SAFETY_ASSURANCE_PROFILE.CURRENTNESS_OR_CHANGE_TRIGGER: Any change to claim, configuration, assumptions, environment or evidence validity.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Defeaters, counterevidence and authorised challenge in assurance
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Critical argumentation, independent review and Assurance 2.0 reforms of confirmatory safety cases.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Actively search for conditions that would defeat a claim, invalidate evidence or reverse a safety decision.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Assurance gathers only confirming evidence and treats unresolved objections as editorial defects.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss after a plausible counter-scenario, adverse test or invalid assumption was ignored or normalised.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Confirmation bias, authority gradients, schedule pressure and challenge without closure suppress disconfirming information.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Record defeaters and contrary evidence, empower technically competent challenge, assign closure criteria and preserve unresolved uncertainty in acceptance.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-consequence or model-sensitive claims, novel systems and changes that invalidate prior assumptions.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a settled low-consequence deterministic claim, one sanity check is enough; adversarial boards add no value.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Psychological/organisational safety for dissent, traceable challenge state and a decision process that can change course.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Challengers need access and non-retaliation; decision authority must answer rather than merely receive objections.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Open objections, negative tests, anomaly trends, premise failures, response quality and whether decisions changed.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces self-confirming assurance and makes uncertainty actionable before deployment.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Independent assessor, workforce/operator, safety board and accountable decision owner.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Performative red teaming, endless objections without decision criteria, retaliation and burying challenges in appendices.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Challenge quality is difficult to measure; more reviewers can repeat the same assumptions or paralyse decisions.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from review sign-off toward explicit defeater logs, confidence arguments and closure/acceptance of unresolved challenges.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A consequential claim remains provisional until material defeaters are eliminated, controlled, or explicitly accepted by the right authority.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A “devil’s advocate” meeting is not required; live disconfirming evidence and authority to act are.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Configuration identity binding for safety evidence
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Configuration management in military/aerospace system safety, software assurance and safety-case practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Bind hazards, assumptions, analyses, tests, approvals and operating limits to an identifiable system configuration and environment.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Apparently green evidence refers to a different build, calibration, supplier component, model, procedure or operating context.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unsafe release or operation based on valid historical evidence that no longer describes the actual system.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Silent drift, untracked field modification, document/code divergence, wrong test article or environment mismatch.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Record decision-relevant configuration identifiers and evidence provenance; verify deployed identity and invalidate/reassess affected claims on divergence.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any safety-relevant change, distributed deployment, supplier substitution or long-lived assurance claim.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a local disposable reversible experiment, identify only the artefact and conditions necessary to reproduce the decisive check.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Controlled baselines, deployment observability, supplier/change notification and an impact model.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Release/operations authority must be able to block unknown or mismatched configurations.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Build/component IDs, calibration, parameters, environment, evidence version, deployment inventory and deviations.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents stale but internally valid evidence from authorising the wrong system.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Configuration manager, release authority, safety case owner, operator and assessor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Identifier bureaucracy without semantic impact, uncontrolled runtime adaptation and false confidence in nominal version labels.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: A hash or baseline name does not prove behavioural equivalence; operational environment and hidden dependencies may still differ.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward machine-linked evidence provenance, deployed-state attestation and assumption/configuration impact graphs.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: No consequential safety claim is reusable without demonstrating that its configuration, environment and assumptions still match.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is identity/equivalence sufficient for the decision; a particular CM database is not required.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Safety impact analysis and proportionate re-assurance after change
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Military/aerospace modification assessment, process management of change, nuclear modification and incremental medical-device assurance.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Classify a change, identify affected hazards/controls/assumptions/interfaces/evidence, reuse unaffected evidence and re-establish affected claims.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A “small” change bypasses safety reasoning, or every change triggers a full undifferentiated re-certification.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from changed behaviour or assumptions; or safety debt/workarounds caused by excessive change burden.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Scope is inferred from file count or label rather than causal reach; indirect interfaces, suppliers and operational context are missed.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Use traceable impact analysis from change to hazards, interactions, constraints and evidence; test the affected frontier and monitor uncertain effects.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Software, hardware, supplier, environment, procedure, security and organisational changes with plausible hazard reach.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A trivial local reversible change with a decisive regression discriminator uses that check and records only the necessary identity.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current baseline, dependency/interface model, hazard state and authority to classify/escalate change.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Change authority must be able to stop release, demand wider evidence and approve bounded reuse.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Diff/configuration identity, changed assumptions, affected tests, operational telemetry, regression and rollback readiness.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves assurance currentness without discarding valid unaffected evidence or freezing improvement.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Change control, release authority, system safety, operator and regulator/certifier.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Form-based classification, hidden cumulative change, reusing stale evidence, certification avoidance and blanket rework.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Incremental assurance depends on accurate impact models; complex adaptive interactions can defeat locality assumptions.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from document change control toward model-linked differential assurance, predetermined change plans and post-change monitoring.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Re-establish exactly the safety claims whose system, assumptions, controls or evidence may have changed; justify both reuse and new work.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A change board is optional; causal impact, authority and current evidence are not.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Living, current and operationally connected assurance
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Through-life safety cases, dynamic safety cases and objectives-driven case-assured regulation.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Maintain claims, evidence, assumptions, hazard controls and operational indicators as the system and context change.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A once-approved case remains nominally valid while configuration, environment, usage, threats or control performance drift.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Operation continues under stale assurance that no longer represents current hazard exposure or control health.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Update latency, disconnected telemetry, alert overload, unowned evidence expiry and dashboards without decision authority.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define change and operational triggers, connect leading evidence to claims, reassess affected arguments and require decision closure.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Long-lived software-intensive, autonomous, security-exposed or operationally adapting systems.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Static assurance can suffice for a stable, bounded, short-lived and readily observed system; update only when a relevant trigger occurs.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable claim architecture, configuration identity, trusted telemetry, trigger thresholds and resourced decision owners.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Owners need authority to restrict, degrade, rollback or re-assure on adverse evidence.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Configuration, control health, incidents/precursors, assumption monitors, evidence expiry and operational-envelope excursions.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces the gap between certification-time belief and operational truth.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, safety case owner, release authority, regulator and maintenance organisation.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Dashboard theatre, noisy triggers, automated circular evidence, alert fatigue and impossible real-time completeness.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Continuous assurance cannot observe unknown hazards and may privilege measurable proxies over causal control state.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from static documents toward event-driven modular re-assurance with explicit evidence freshness and human authority.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Assurance remains valid only while named configuration, assumptions, controls and evidence are current; relevant changes trigger bounded reassessment.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Continuous document editing is not required; current decision-relevant assurance state is.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Independent assessment and IV&V where consequence warrants
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Military/aerospace independent verification and validation, certification and nuclear independent review.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Use technically competent assessors outside the delivery decision chain to challenge high-consequence claims and evidence.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: The producing team is the sole judge of its own assumptions, implementation and verification, or independent review becomes duplicate checklist work.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Undetected systematic defect, optimistic interpretation or conflicted acceptance in consequential systems.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Shared oracles, insufficient access, ceremonial sign-off, late review and organisational independence without informational independence.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define risk-based scope, give assessors evidence/tool/access rights, seek independent information and close material findings before acceptance.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Catastrophic or irreversible failure conditions, novel technology, weak testability, conflicted suppliers or mandated domains.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Routine peer review or one deterministic check is sufficient for low-consequence reversible work; separate IV&V should not trigger by label alone.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Competence, access, independence, clear claim scope and response authority.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The assessor must be able to report to an authority that can change design, release or operation.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Independent defect findings, evidence provenance, unresolved dissent, retest results and configuration coverage.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Creates a second opportunity to expose common delivery blind spots and conflicts before irreversible commitment.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Risk acceptor, certification authority, programme executive and operator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Expensive late paperwork, adversarial handoff, duplicated evidence and false inference that separation guarantees independence.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Controlled multiversion evidence and assurance failures show that nominal independence can remain correlated.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward consequence-based scoping, early continuous involvement and explicit informational-independence analysis.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Deploy independent assessment only where its distinct information and challenge authority justify cost, and measure it by decisions/findings rather than signatures.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A separate organisation is not the property; independently informative challenge is.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Evidence triangulation and targeted formal verification
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Formal-methods research, IV&V, quantitative analysis and assurance-case synthesis.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Match claim-critical uncertainties to evidence methods with complementary strengths, including formal proof where a precise model materially reduces uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Testing alone misses rare state spaces, proof establishes the wrong model, or many weak methods are combined without a claim-specific rationale.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unsafe acceptance after untested corner states, invalid formal assumptions or common evidence blind spots.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Model–implementation gap, specification error, unqualified tools, oracle weakness and evidence dependence.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: For each consequential claim, select the least set of analyses/tests/inspections/operational evidence that attacks distinct failure modes; prove only tractable decisive properties.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Complex logic, concurrency, control laws, protection functions or rare combinations where exhaustive empirical testing is infeasible.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use direct execution, inspection or deterministic testing when it fully settles a simple claim; formalisation must earn its cost.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Precise property and model, validated abstraction, configuration mapping, trustworthy tools and a decision consumer.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Assurance authority decides where proof/test diversity is necessary and owns residual model risk.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Proof obligations, model assumptions, code/configuration correspondence, test coverage and operational anomalies.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Improves state-space coverage while exposing which uncertainty each evidence item actually reduces.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Designer, verifier, safety case owner and independent assessor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Proof theatre, unverifiable models, tool-chain dependence, duplicated evidence and formal work disconnected from hazard decisions.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Formal proof establishes only the modelled property under assumptions; outcome superiority over disciplined testing is context dependent.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from “formal versus testing” toward claim-driven portfolios, model validation and explicit evidence-dependence reasoning.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use formal methods selectively where a precise hazard-linked property and abstraction make them decisively informative, then triangulate model correspondence.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A proof certificate is not a safety claim about the physical system without validated assumptions and configuration linkage.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Joint safety–security analysis for cyber-physical control
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Functional safety, automotive cybersecurity, medical-device cybersecurity and nuclear safety/security interface guidance.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Analyse malicious, accidental and mixed pathways that alter safety-critical control, feedback, availability, configuration or recovery.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Safety assumes benign faults while security changes disable controls, spoof feedback or make a safe shutdown unavailable.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Physical or health loss caused or amplified by compromised digital/organisational control.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Separate teams use incompatible assets, threat/hazard models, timing assumptions and change controls; security fixes introduce new safety hazards.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Share system/control boundaries, identify safety consequences of threats and security consequences of safety controls, coordinate mitigations and changes.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Networked, updateable, remotely supported, autonomous or adversarially exposed safety-relevant systems.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not impose a full threat programme on an isolated trivial reversible function with no plausible adversarial safety pathway.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Shared architecture/configuration view, threat and hazard expertise, coordinated authority and secure observability.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Safety and security owners need a joint escalation/acceptance path; neither may unilaterally break the other control objective.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Security events, control/feedback integrity, patch/configuration status, availability, anomalies and attack-path assumptions.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Closes a modern interaction class in which security compromise becomes a safety cause or safety control expands attack surface.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Safety, security, operations, supplier and risk-acceptance authorities.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Duplicated registers, safety/security priority conflict, secrecy blocking evidence and emergency patching without safety impact analysis.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Integrated methods and comparative effectiveness evidence are still developing; total model completeness is impossible.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward shared cyber-physical control models, coordinated change assurance and explicit conflict resolution.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Co-engineer safety and security whenever they share control, feedback, configuration or availability dependencies; keep domain analyses complementary.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A combined workshop or merged document is optional; the shared causal paths and authority are not.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Actionable hazard detection and alarm burden control
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Process protection, aviation/medical human factors and alarm-management practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Detect hazardous or degraded states early enough for a named consumer to take an effective action, while controlling nuisance and overload.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Detection is counted as control although no one can interpret or act on it, or excessive alarms hide the critical signal.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Uncontained hazard due to missed, late, stale, ambiguous or ignored warning; secondary loss from needless stops.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Poor sensor coverage, threshold design, prioritisation, mode context, alarm floods and absent response authority.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Link each safety-significant alarm to hazard, timing, decision, response and confirmation; monitor false/missed alarm performance and rationalise burden.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Hazards requiring detection before irreversible progression, especially remote or highly automated processes.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Direct physical prevention or immediate observation may be cheaper than alarms; do not alert when no safe action exists.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Detectable precursor, sufficient response time, reliable signal semantics, trained/authorised consumer and maintained sensors.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The receiver needs authority and resources to diagnose, stop, isolate or escalate; alarm ownership must be explicit.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Detection probability/latency, false/nuisance rate, acknowledgement, action completion, alarm floods and sensor health.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts hidden degradation into timely preventive or containment action without overwhelming operators.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, automated safety controller, maintenance and emergency response.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Alarm fatigue, automation bias, disabled alarms, alert storms, threshold gaming and no-action dashboards.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: More detection can reduce safety when attention and response capacity are saturated; alarm counts are poor proxies.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from instrument installation toward hazard-linked performance requirements, prioritisation, human factors and consumer/action verification.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: An alarm is justified only when its signal is trustworthy, timely, discriminating and connected to an effective authorised response.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A dashboard tile or alarm count is ceremony without a live decision and burden budget.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Containment, isolation and emergency stop with state confirmation
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Process emergency shutdown/isolation, interlocks and system-safety fail-safe design.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: When prevention fails or a hazard is detected, interrupt propagation, isolate energy/material/control paths and confirm the intended safe condition.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A stop request or valve command is treated as containment although actuation, isolation integrity or process response is unconfirmed.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Escalating release, collision, energy transfer or public exposure after a failed prevention layer.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Actuator failure, shared utility loss, inaccessible isolation, delayed action, feedback echo and unsafe stop sequence.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define containment objective and time, provide independent actuation/feedback where warranted, test the whole path and restrict operation on degraded protection.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Hazards whose progression can still be bounded after detection and before irreversible loss.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a local reversible state, a direct stop and immediate observation may suffice; do not add emergency machinery without a credible propagation path.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Reachable safe/contained state, sufficient time, maintained actuation and feedback, and known interactions with mission/availability.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Controller/operator must have stop authority; restart authority is separate and requires restoration evidence.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Command receipt, actuator position, process state, leak/energy isolation, residual inventory and containment integrity.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Limits consequence when elimination and prevention are incomplete and creates a recoverable boundary.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, automated protection, emergency response and restart authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: False assumption of fail-safe position, bypasses, inaccessible controls, common utility failure and emergency stop creating a worse hazard.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: HSE safety alerts show nominal safe-position claims can fail physically; fail-safe is not universal where service continuity prevents harm.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward end-to-end state confirmation, periodic proof testing, partial/degraded modes and explicit stop-versus-continue tradeoffs.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Containment is achieved only when the hazardous process state is demonstrably bounded, not when a command is issued.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Emergency-stop hardware is context-specific; verified propagation control is the property.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Context-sensitive fail-safe, fail-operational and graceful-degradation design
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Reliability/system-safety fail-safe design, nuclear/aviation continuity requirements and modern automated-system degradation modes.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Choose whether to stop, continue, isolate or degrade based on which state minimises credible loss under the actual failure and mission context.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: “Fail safe” is interpreted as always shut down, or availability is prioritised without bounded degraded operation.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss caused either by hazardous continued operation or by removal of a service necessary to protect life/mission.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Wrong safe-state assumption, hidden mode transition, degraded function outside envelope, common-mode protection loss or unannounced capability reduction.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define mode-specific safe/degraded envelopes, transition logic, time limits, operator authority and feedback; prove both continuation and stopping hazards.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Systems where stopping and continuing can each be hazardous: aircraft, medical support, nuclear cooling, transport and emergency services.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For noncritical reversible functions, stop cleanly and recover normally; elaborate degradation architectures are unnecessary.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit mission/loss model, reliable mode detection, bounded degraded capability and containment/recovery path.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Automation and operators need defined transition/override authority; degraded operation must have an accountable expiry/recovery owner.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Mode, remaining capability, environmental demand, barrier health, time in degraded state and operator comprehension.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Avoids universal shutdown dogma while preventing unbounded “limp home” operation.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System architect, operator, mission owner and safety authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Mode confusion, latent degradation, excessive complexity, optimistic remaining-capability estimates and normalisation of temporary modes.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Continued service can be necessary for safety, but fail-operational complexity and human understanding can introduce new hazards.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from binary fail-safe rules toward hazard-specific degraded envelopes, graceful degradation and explicit transition/recovery assurance.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Select and assure the lowest-loss response for each credible condition, with observable bounded degraded operation and timely recovery.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A named “safe state” is not automatically safe across modes; the underlying loss comparison and controlled transition are the property.

SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROLLER: The decision owner or engineering function responsible for this property.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROLLED_PROCESS: The design, operation, change or assurance process in which the hazard can arise.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.SAFETY_CONSTRAINT: The system shall not enter or remain in the hazardous condition addressed by Context-sensitive fail-safe, fail-operational and graceful-degradation design.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.CONTROL_ACTION: Define mode-specific safe/degraded envelopes, transition logic, time limits, operator authority and feedback; prove both continuation and stopping hazards.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK: Mode, remaining capability, environmental demand, barrier health, time in degraded state and operator comprehension.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.PROCESS_MODEL_ASSUMPTION: Explicit mission/loss model, reliable mode detection, bounded degraded capability and containment/recovery path.
SAFETY_CONTROL_LOOP_PROFILE.DELAY_OR_OBSERVABILITY_RISK: Delay, missing data or stale configuration can leave the controller acting on an obsolete model.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Recovery, rollback and restart only after restored safety constraints
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Nuclear operating limits, process isolation/restart, software rollback and through-life system-safety practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Separate containment from recovery and restart; restore constraints, configuration and observability before returning to service.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Service restoration or command success is treated as proof that the hazard and its causal mechanism are controlled.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Recurrence, latent damaged state or new loss during premature restart or unsafe rollback.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Pressure to resume, incomplete diagnosis, incompatible rollback, untested repairs, reset alarms and missing proof of barrier restoration.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define recovery objectives, known-safe configuration, validation/proof tests, staged restart, monitoring and explicit restart authority.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Consequential incidents, emergency stops, failed changes, degraded modes and repairs that can leave latent hazard.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A trivial reversible action can be retried after direct verification; no recovery board is needed.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Recoverable baseline, rollback compatibility, diagnostic evidence, barrier tests and an escalation path when state is uncertain.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Restart authority must be distinct from the person merely restoring service and able to demand continued restriction.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Constraint/barrier status, configuration identity, residual damage, test results, anomaly trend and staged operating feedback.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents recurrence and converts emergency action into verified restoration rather than optimistic reset.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operations, maintenance, release/change authority, incident owner and safety/risk acceptor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Checklist reset, rollback to vulnerable/unsafe configuration, restart pressure, test-induced risk and permanent temporary controls.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Proof testing can itself be hazardous or incomplete; exact recovery architecture is highly domain specific.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward explicit recovery states, staged return, rollback assurance, compensating controls and post-restart monitoring.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Recovery is complete only when relevant safety constraints and feedback are re-established and an authorised owner accepts the remaining uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A restart checklist is optional; demonstrable restored control and separate authority are not.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Bounded emergency or temporary risk acceptance with compensating controls
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Military/aerospace waivers, nuclear technical specifications, process-management-of-change and operational deviation practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Permit exceptional operation only within explicit scope, time, configuration and compensating-control limits, with expiry and restoration obligations.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A temporary deviation silently becomes normal operation, or emergency pressure removes all hazard discrimination.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss while a known protection is unavailable or while an exceptional configuration accumulates unexamined risk.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Weak authority, indefinite waiver, ineffective compensation, changed exposure, handoff failure and no restoration owner.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: State the impaired control and hazard, select credible compensation, limit exposure/time, monitor conditions, assign expiry and require reauthorisation or restoration.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Urgent mission, repair, emergency change or safety-critical-service continuity where immediate full restoration is impossible.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not create a waiver for trivial work already inside ordinary authority, and do not use temporary acceptance to avoid feasible permanent correction.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known hazard/control state, feasible compensation, monitorable envelope, restoration plan and authority commensurate with consequence.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: A named emergency/risk authority must own the decision; operators need stop authority if compensation degrades.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Time/exposure, compensating-control health, changed conditions, incidents, handoffs and restoration progress.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Allows necessary bounded operation without hiding the increased risk or normalising impairment.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operations, emergency command, maintenance/change owner and residual-risk authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Waiver culture, deadline renewal, paper compensations, authority diffusion and production pressure redefining emergencies.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Temporary acceptance is especially susceptible to normalisation and may externalise harm; some hazards should not be accepted.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward machine-visible expiry, exposure budgets, independent monitoring and explicit restoration/re-acceptance criteria.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Exceptional operation is safe enough only within an observable, time/configuration-bounded envelope whose compensating controls and authority remain current.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A waiver form is not the property; bounded exposure, live compensation, expiry and restoration are.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Incident, near-miss and precursor reporting connected to learning
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Industrial accident reporting, aviation voluntary reporting, healthcare safety reporting and precursor-analysis programmes.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Capture adverse events, close calls and weak signals before severe loss, protect reporting where appropriate and route information to hazard/control decisions.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Zero reports are read as zero risk, or reports accumulate without triage, causal analysis, feedback or action.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Repeated or escalating loss because precursor evidence was suppressed, fragmented, misclassified or never consumed.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Blame fear, reporting burden, denominator changes, selection bias, weak taxonomy, alert flooding and no authorised action owner.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define safety-relevant reportability, protect good-faith disclosure, prioritise by credible hazard/control degradation, investigate proportionately and feed actions/status back.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Operational systems with sparse severe events, latent failures, weak signals or learning distributed across workers/users.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For an immediately observed trivial defect already corrected and deterministically verified, a lightweight record or no separate report may be appropriate.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Accessible channel, just reporting conditions, triage competence, hazard linkage and a consumer able to change design or operation.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Reporting recipients require authority or an escalation path; reporters need protection from inappropriate retaliation while reckless conduct remains separately governed.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Report volume and exposure denominator, severity/precursor linkage, time to triage/action, repeat events, closure quality and reporter feedback.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Expands observable evidence beyond rare accidents and can reveal degraded controls before irreversible loss.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operations, safety management, designers, regulators/investigators and corrective-action owners.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Reporting quotas, count-based culture metrics, duplicate low-value reports, confidentiality barriers, underreporting and recommendation inflation.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Near-miss counts are strongly incentive- and exposure-dependent; not every near miss predicts catastrophe and reporting alone does not improve safety.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from incident counting toward protected reporting, precursor/control-state interpretation, causal triage and verified learning loops.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Collect only information with a plausible hazard/control consumer, interpret counts with exposure and incentives, and close the loop through action or justified no-action.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A reporting portal is not the property; observable weak signals, protected transmission and decision closure are.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Multi-factor causal investigation grounded in local rationality
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Human-factors critique of “human error”, Reason/local-rationality work, systems accident models and modern RCA reforms.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Reconstruct how technical, human, organisational and environmental conditions made actions locally reasonable and combined into loss.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Investigation stops at operator error, one root cause or rule violation and therefore controls only the last visible act.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Recurrence because upstream design, feedback, workload, authority, incentives, interfaces and defences remain unchanged.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Hindsight bias, blame seeking, evidence loss, linear storytelling, causal overreach and recommendation lists not linked to mechanisms.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Preserve evidence, build competing causal scenarios, test counterfactual control changes, distinguish contributing mechanisms and stop when additional evidence no longer changes action.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Serious incidents, recurring near misses and unexplained control/interaction failures.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A simple, directly observed and deterministically reproducible defect can be corrected without an elaborate sociotechnical investigation.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Timely access to technical/organisational evidence, multidisciplinary competence and separation between learning and inappropriate punishment.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Investigators need independence and access; organisations must empower consumers to change upstream controls rather than only retrain operators.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Timeline/state reconstruction, alternative explanations, missing/stale feedback, goal conflicts, control deficiencies, action implementation and recurrence.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Produces countermeasures aimed at causal mechanisms rather than scapegoats or generic reminders.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Investigator, design/operations authority, regulator and corrective-action owner.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Infinite causal chains, fashionable systems diagrams, weak counterfactuals, no root prioritisation and recommendations beyond available evidence.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Systems analyses remain judgement-sensitive; “no root cause” must not become refusal to identify controllable mechanisms or accountability.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from single-cause RCA toward multiple interacting mechanisms, local rationality, control deficiencies and action-centred RCA².
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Investigate until the credible causal mechanisms needed to select and verify controls are sufficiently discriminated, without treating error labels as explanations.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A specific RCA diagram is optional; evidence-preserving causal discrimination and action linkage are the property.

EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH: HIGH — origin and transmission are documented in primary or authoritative historical sources.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.FORMAL_OR_MODEL_STRENGTH: MODERATE — mechanism is coherent but depends on model scope and assumptions.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.ACCIDENT_CASE_STRENGTH: HIGH — major investigations repeatedly identify authority, incentive, communication and adaptation mechanisms.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_STRENGTH: MODERATE — observational evidence is substantial; causal identification and transfer remain difficult.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.DOMAIN_PRACTICE_STRENGTH: HIGH — established in mature high-consequence practice when properly scoped.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.STANDARD_OR_REGULATORY_STRENGTH: HIGH — required or recognised in one or more authoritative regimes; this is practice authority, not optimality proof.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH: MODERATE_TO_HIGH — mechanism transfers when the same hazard/control conditions exist; artefacts do not automatically transfer.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY: HIGH — value depends on boundary, model, data, authority, independence and current configuration.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH: MODERATE — implementation failures and scope critiques materially constrain use.
EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.SOURCE_BASIS: Primary: S063, S064, S076, S077, S109, S110; critical/contrary: S066, S107.

PROPERTIES.EMPIRICAL_OR_DOMAIN_EVIDENCE: Major accident investigations and systematic systems-method reviews repeatedly identify multi-level contributing mechanisms.
PROPERTIES.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Comparative evidence that one systems method yields better prevention than another remains limited and retrospective causal claims are vulnerable to hindsight.
PROPERTIES.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What stopping rule best balances additional causal discrimination against post-hoc narrative growth and delayed action?

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Corrective-action ownership, implementation and effectiveness verification
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Accident-investigation recommendation systems and RCA² reform of analysis without action.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Convert a causal finding into a hazard-relevant action with a responsible owner, due state, implementation evidence and effectiveness/recurrence check.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: An investigation or recommendation is counted as closed when issued, accepted, trained or documented rather than when the causal control improves.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Repeat loss because recommendations have no capable consumer, address symptoms, are not implemented or create new hazards.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Owner ambiguity, action inflation, output metrics, weak causal link, status self-report and no post-implementation observation.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: For each material mechanism, specify the control change and expected indicator, assign authority/resources, verify implementation, test effectiveness and monitor recurrence/side effects.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Material incidents, recurring precursors, audit findings and accepted safety recommendations.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a trivial directly fixed defect, the repair plus decisive regression check can close the action without a separate tracker.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Causal mechanism sufficiently understood, feasible action, named empowered owner, current configuration and measurable verification condition.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The owner must control resources/design/operations or have escalation; the investigator should not declare effectiveness solely from paperwork.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Implementation evidence, changed control performance, recurrence/precursors, side effects, overdue status and reason for closure.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Ensures learning changes the system and distinguishes action completion from risk reduction.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design/operations management, regulator/investigator, safety board and affected workforce/users.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Recommendation proliferation, weak “retrain/rewrite” actions, closure gaming, orphaned recommendations and unmeasured displacement of risk.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Effectiveness is hard to infer for rare events; absence of recurrence over short exposure is weak evidence.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from report issuance toward SMARTER causal actions, public status classification, implementation verification and outcome/precursor monitoring.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: No safety finding is closed merely by documentation: close the causal-control loop or explicitly record why no further action has decision value.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: An action database is optional; an empowered consumer and verified causal effect are not.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Leading indicators tied to explicit hazards and control performance
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Process-safety precursor analysis, nuclear maintenance monitoring, organisational migration models and resilience-oriented monitoring.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Monitor conditions that causally bear on barrier, control, assumption or exposure state before lagging loss occurs.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Generic activity counts, safety-culture scores or injury rates are treated as proof that high-consequence controls work.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Latent degradation and migration toward hazard boundaries remain invisible until a severe event.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Proxy gaming, indicator drift, Goodhart effects, missing denominators, unvalidated causal link and dashboard overload.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Derive a small set of indicators from the hazard/control model, state expected direction and threshold, validate against operations and pair every threshold with a decision.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Sparse-event, latent-failure or slowly degrading systems where incident rates provide delayed or statistically weak feedback.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use direct control-state inspection when available; do not create proxy metrics where a deterministic discriminator already answers the question.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit causal hypothesis, reliable data and exposure denominator, stable semantics and authorised response.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: An owner must be able to inspect, restrict, maintain or redesign on adverse trends and to retire misleading indicators.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Barrier availability, overdue proof tests, excursions, workload/override patterns, weak signals, exposure and decision response.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides earlier evidence of eroding safety margins than severe-event counts alone.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operations, maintenance, safety management and risk authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Metric fixation, target manipulation, false reassurance, excessive alerting and treating correlation as causation.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Evidence linking broad culture/leading scores to accident prevention is mixed; indicators are model-dependent and can be gamed.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from lagging counts toward hazard-specific control-health and assumption indicators with explicit consumers and periodic validation.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A leading indicator is retained only when its causal relevance, denominator, decision threshold and consumer remain credible.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A KPI dashboard is not a property; timely control-state information that changes action is.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Organisational control, incentives and production-pressure analysis
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Major accident investigations, Rasmussen boundary migration, high-reliability studies and systems accident models.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Treat budgets, schedules, staffing, communication, authority, contracting and performance pressures as parts of the safety control structure.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Safety is delegated to frontline compliance while upstream decisions systematically weaken barriers, suppress evidence or reward risk-taking.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Catastrophic loss arising from normal organisational adaptation, resource choices and authority/information failures.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Conflicting goals, diffused responsibility, normalisation, weak feedback upward, authority gradients and metrics that externalise risk.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Map decision/control paths and incentives, identify where authority and safety information diverge, install escalation/stop rights and monitor boundary migration.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Complex organisations, outsourced supply chains, long operations, high schedule pressure and hazards spanning multiple management levels.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not invent culture programmes for a simple local technical defect; correct the direct mechanism and verify it.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Access to real work and decision data, leadership willingness to expose tradeoffs, protected reporting and feasible upstream controls.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Leaders controlling resources and priorities must own safety consequences; frontline responsibility requires matching authority.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Staffing/workload, deferred maintenance, waivers, schedule overrides, unresolved findings, reporting quality, barrier health and escalation outcomes.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Controls recurring conditions that make otherwise competent local action unsafe and prevents blame displacement.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Executives, programme/operations management, regulators, workforce and system safety.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Vague culture rhetoric, retrospective moralising, endless organisational diagrams and accountability dilution.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Organisational causation is difficult to quantify and broad systems explanations can obscure specific decision responsibility.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from “safety culture” exhortation toward observable control, incentive, resource, feedback and authority mechanisms.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Analyse and change the upstream decisions and feedback loops that shape risk, while retaining named accountability for controllable choices.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A culture survey or values statement is not the property; decision-relevant organisational control is.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Supplier and contractor boundary assurance with change notification
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Defence/aerospace system-safety programmes, medical-device supply control, nuclear modification and process contractor management.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Preserve safety requirements, assumptions, evidence, configuration identity and notification duties across organisational boundaries.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: The integrator assumes supplier compliance establishes system safety, or a supplier changes a safety-relevant component/process without impact analysis.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from hidden component behaviour, interface mismatch, counterfeit/substituted part, evidence opacity or divided authority.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Contract gaps, proprietary barriers, incompatible hazard models, unmanaged subcontractors and responsibility without control.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Allocate hazard-linked obligations and interface assumptions, require evidence and change/anomaly notification, verify integration and retain integrator accountability.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Safety-relevant purchased software/hardware, outsourced operations/maintenance and multi-tier supply chains.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Commodity low-consequence components with a decisive acceptance test can use that test rather than imposing a full supplier safety system.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Clear technical/contract boundary, component criticality, integration testability, configuration provenance and enforceable notification terms.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The integrator must retain system-level acceptance authority; suppliers need authority/resources to disclose and correct defects.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Supplier versions, deviations, anomalies, process/evidence changes, interface conformance and field performance.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Closes information and control gaps that component certification or procurement paperwork alone cannot cover.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Integrator, supplier quality/safety, procurement, configuration/change authority and operator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Flow-down paperwork, supplier scorecards, proprietary evidence dead ends, duplicated audits and false transfer of responsibility.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Contracts cannot reveal unknown interactions or guarantee candour; excessive requirements can reduce supplier diversity and agility.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward risk-tiered supplier assurance, software bills/provenance, continuous notification and integration-focused evidence reuse.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Match supplier assurance to system consequence and interface uncertainty, but keep the integrator responsible for composed safety.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A supplier certificate is not the property; current boundary evidence, notification and integration control are.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Operational monitoring and adaptive safety-envelope governance
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Operational limits, dynamic risk monitoring, resilience engineering and continuous assurance.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Monitor whether operation remains inside validated safety constraints and adapt restrictions or assurance when environment, demand or performance changes.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Certification-time assumptions remain fixed while operations migrate, or adaptive response changes behaviour without bounded authority/evidence.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Loss from envelope excursion, unobserved degradation, novel context or adaptation that invalidates prior assurance.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Incomplete state sensing, concept drift, threshold gaming, delayed feedback, adaptation beyond authority and false belief that monitoring covers unknowns.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define observable envelope variables and assumptions, detect excursions, restrict/degrade or learn within authorised bounds, and re-assure material adaptations.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Long-lived, variable-environment, autonomous or rapidly updated systems where predeployment evidence cannot cover all operational states.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Stable bounded systems with direct deterministic protection may only need periodic checks; continuous dashboards are unnecessary.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Validated envelope, trustworthy telemetry, anomaly/assumption monitors, safe fallback and authority to intervene or revise constraints.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Operations must have stop/degrade authority; adaptation outside the assured envelope requires explicit change/risk authority.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Envelope variables, assumption validity, control effectiveness, anomalies, drift, exposure and recovery performance.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Maintains safety under real-world variability and reveals where assurance no longer applies.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, autonomy supervisor, safety case owner, release authority and regulator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Monitoring theatre, alert overload, unsafe online experimentation, proxy drift and adaptation masking deteriorating margins.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Resilience concepts can be vague and monitoring cannot guarantee discovery of unknown hazards; intervention itself can destabilise service.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward runtime assurance, explicit operational design domains, dynamic cases and bounded adaptive control rather than unrestricted flexibility.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Permit adaptation only inside an observable, hazard-linked and authority-bounded envelope, with fallback and change-aware re-assurance.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: “Resilience” language or a dashboard is not enough; explicit constraints, feedback, decisions and limits are required.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Cheap authoritative discriminator for low-consequence reversible work
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Tailoring provisions in mature aerospace/system-safety guidance and goal-setting, risk-informed regulation; synthesized anti-bureaucracy property.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: When a narrow, deterministic and authoritative check settles a local safety question, use it directly and escalate only on failed assumptions or wider consequence.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Full hazard-analysis, assurance-case and review machinery is applied despite zero expected decision value, consuming attention and provoking bypass.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Indirect safety loss from delayed repair/service, attention dilution and procedural noncompliance; wasted cost without improved discrimination.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Process is triggered by label, document type or change count rather than credible loss, reversibility and uncertainty.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Classify consequence and scope, apply the decisive test/guard, record only necessary identity/result, and define escalation triggers for ambiguity or coupling.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Local, cheap, reversible, immediately observable work with stable assumptions and an authoritative deterministic discriminator.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: This property is itself the cheap path; it does not apply when consequence, irreversibility, coupling, latent effects or uncertain interactions are material.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: The discriminator actually covers the safety question, the result is observable and rollback/containment remains available.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Ordinary engineering authority may act within bounded delegation; anyone detecting scope expansion can escalate.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Check result, exact local configuration, rollback success if used and evidence that assumptions did not widen.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves safety attention and delivery speed while preventing ceremonial controls from crowding out consequential work.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Engineer/operator, change authority and safety function defining the tailoring boundary.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Under-classification, calling uncertain work “reversible”, hidden propagation and using cheap path to evade inconvenient scrutiny.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Tailoring can be gamed and no deterministic check is authoritative outside its proven scope.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from blanket exemptions toward explicit non-trigger conditions, bounded delegation and automatic escalation on uncertainty/coupling.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the least costly discriminator that conclusively controls the credible loss; never perform a safety ritual solely because its template exists.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: No special artefact is required beyond sufficient evidence of scope, result and escalation conditions.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Retirement of controls whose hazard or decision consumer has disappeared
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Living assurance, management of change, alarm rationalisation and adaptive safety-management practice.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Periodically remove, merge or redesign a control, alarm, metric or artefact when its hazard, causal mechanism, assumption or authorised consumer no longer exists.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Legacy controls accumulate indefinitely, obscure live hazards, conflict with current work and are preserved because removal itself is procedurally difficult.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Safety attention dilution, alarm fatigue, workaround, unavailable service or false belief that an obsolete control remains protective.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: No ownership/expiry, changed architecture, orphaned requirement, vanished consumer and process incentives rewarding control count.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Require each control to retain a hazard/constraint link, owner, consumer and effectiveness signal; decommission through impact analysis and verify no residual dependency.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Long-lived systems with substantial change, accumulated waivers, alarms, checklists, reports or certification artefacts.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not run a retirement review for a transient local check that naturally ends with the task.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current hazard/configuration model, evidence of non-use or replacement, dependency analysis and authority to remove safely.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The control owner and affected risk/operations authority must approve removal; users need a path to reveal hidden dependence.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Consumer use, action triggered, false-positive/bypass burden, control effectiveness, dependencies and post-retirement anomalies.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Keeps the safety system sparse, current and credible and returns attention to live hazards.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Control owner, operator, assurance/change authority and affected decision consumer.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Premature removal, undocumented informal dependence, metric gaming and “cleanup” that erases historical evidence.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Absence of recent activation may reflect successful prevention or rare demand, not obsolescence.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward expiry metadata, consumer/use telemetry, periodic rationalisation and change-aware decommissioning.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Live decision consumer for every safety artefact and control
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: System-safety programme management, safety-case practice and criticism of recommendation/paper assurance.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Create and maintain a safety artefact only when a named person/process uses it to design, accept, operate, stop, recover or learn.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Hazard logs, matrices, reports, models and reviews are produced for compliance without changing any authorised decision.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Uncontrolled hazard masked by document completion, plus attention/cost displaced from effective controls.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: No consumer, no authority, unclear decision threshold, stale update cycle and metrics rewarding artefact quantity.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: State the decision, consumer, trigger and required information before producing the artefact; observe use and retire or redesign if it does not change action.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any recurring safety analysis, review, metric, report, case or control.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not create a separate artefact when the decisive information is already embedded in an authoritative engineering/operational control.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Real decision need, current evidence, accessible representation and consumer authority.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: The consumer must be able to act or escalate; the producer cannot substitute document delivery for control.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Decision made, challenge raised, action/acceptance changed, use frequency, stale age and unresolved consumer feedback.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Strips ceremony while preserving durable decision memory and accountability.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Designer, operator, risk acceptor, reviewer/investigator and regulator.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Artificially naming a consumer, rubber-stamp use, hidden secondary consumers and deleting records needed for future learning.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Some assurance artefacts serve latent legal/public accountability and rare future decisions, so immediate use alone is not sufficient.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from deliverable compliance toward decision-first assurance, machine-linked traceability and consumer/expiry tests.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every artefact must earn existence through a current or credibly latent consequential decision and an owner who can act on it.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Hazard-control hierarchy favouring elimination and engineered control
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Industrial hygiene/occupational safety hierarchy, military system-safety design order and standards safety principles.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Prefer elimination, substitution, inherently safer design and engineered prevention before warnings, procedures, training or personal response where feasible.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Administrative controls are accepted because they are cheap to document even though the hazard can be designed out or physically bounded.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Preventable exposure or catastrophic demand on humans/procedures after a feasible stronger control was omitted.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Cost/schedule bias, late analysis, overconfidence in training, new hazards introduced by redesign and absolute hierarchy use without context.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Search controls in strength order, document why stronger options are infeasible or harmful, and monitor residual lower-level controls.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Identified hazards with feasible design, substitution, guarding, interlock, isolation or exposure-reduction options.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No hierarchy exercise is needed when the hazard is absent or a simple direct constraint already eliminates it.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Early design influence, feasible alternatives, system-level tradeoff analysis and authority/resources to change architecture.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Design/risk authority must be able to reject administrative substitution for feasible engineering control.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Hazard presence, barrier demand, human/procedural dependence, bypass, exposure and side effects of stronger controls.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces dependence on perfect behaviour and recurring procedural compliance.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Designer, operations, occupational/process safety and risk acceptor.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Rigid hierarchy that ignores mission/secondary risk, “elimination” shifting hazard elsewhere and engineered controls with hidden common modes.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: No control class is infallible; engineered automation can create interaction hazards and fail-operational contexts complicate the order.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from slogans toward hazard-specific option analysis, prevention-through-design and monitored combinations.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Eliminate or physically constrain credible hazards where practicable; justify reliance on weaker human/procedural layers and analyse the hazards controls create.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A hierarchy poster is ceremony; actual design-option search and justified residual dependence are the property.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Safety margins, operating envelopes and boundary separation
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Structural/aerospace margins, nuclear operating limits, process safe operating envelopes and Rasmussen boundary models.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Maintain measurable separation between normal operation and hazardous thresholds, including uncertainty, degradation and response time.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Operation is permitted exactly at a nominal limit, or a margin is treated as static despite model error, ageing, environment and coupling.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Abrupt transition into an unrecoverable hazardous state after small variation, delay or latent degradation.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Unknown boundary, optimistic model, cumulative erosion, hidden interactions, production pressure and margin consumed by change.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Define hazard-linked limits and uncertainty allowance, instrument relevant variables, restrict excursions and reassess margins after change/degradation.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-energy, structural, thermal, control or capacity hazards with identifiable boundaries and cliff-edge consequences.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a low-consequence reversible state with immediate deterministic feedback, ordinary tolerance checks may suffice.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: A credible boundary model, calibrated measurement, operational authority and recovery/containment before limit crossing.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Operators/controllers must be able to reduce demand, stop or degrade; change authority owns margin allocation.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Distance to limit, uncertainty, rate of approach, ageing/degradation, excursions, recovery time and barrier availability.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides time and robustness against uncertainty rather than relying on perfect threshold prediction.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, operator, maintenance, regulator and risk authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Arbitrary factors, margin hoarding, false precision, hidden multidimensional boundaries and workarounds around over-conservative limits.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Margins can mask design weakness or reduce necessary service; not all sociotechnical hazards have a scalar boundary.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward multidimensional envelopes, real-time margin monitoring, explicit uncertainty and change-controlled allocation.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Maintain enough observable separation from hazardous boundaries to absorb credible uncertainty and response latency, while revising limits when evidence changes.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A fixed safety factor is domain-specific; controlled separation and margin evidence are the property.

PROPERTIES.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit assumption validity and monitoring
PROPERTIES.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Safety cases, STPA process models, change assessment and dynamic risk/continuous assurance.
PROPERTIES.ORIGINAL_FORM: Make decision-critical assumptions about environment, interfaces, users, independence, data, demand and controls explicit and monitor or revalidate them.
PROPERTIES.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Evidence remains apparently valid after an unstated premise changes or was never true in operation.
PROPERTIES.LOSS_OR_HAZARD: Unsafe behaviour outside the analysed context, common-mode failure or false assurance caused by premise drift.
PROPERTIES.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Hidden assumptions, non-observable premises, too many unprioritised assumptions and monitoring the same source that created the assumption.
PROPERTIES.MECHANISM: Identify claim-critical assumptions, assign evidence/owner/validity period, monitor observable ones and trigger restriction or reassessment on violation.
PROPERTIES.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Novel, changing, autonomous, outsourced or environment-sensitive systems and any reused safety evidence.
PROPERTIES.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not create a register for obvious transient facts already enforced by a deterministic check; record only assumptions whose failure changes a decision.
PROPERTIES.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Claim/hazard model, observable discriminators or periodic revalidation, configuration linkage and action authority.
PROPERTIES.AUTHORITY_OR_CONTROL_PRECONDITIONS: Assumption owners and operators must be able to restrict use, escalate or change the case when validity is uncertain.
PROPERTIES.REQUIRED_FEEDBACK_OR_OBSERVABILITY: Premise status, environmental range, interface/provider behaviour, data drift, independence evidence and violations.
PROPERTIES.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Turns hidden scope limits into testable/revisable control information and supports safe evidence reuse.
PROPERTIES.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Safety case owner, system architect, operations, supplier and change authority.
PROPERTIES.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Assumption-log bloat, tautologies, unmonitorable claims, green dashboards from correlated telemetry and no response to violation.
PROPERTIES.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Unknown unknowns remain outside the register and monitoring can be circular or lagging.
PROPERTIES.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from contextual footnotes toward critical-assumption ownership, runtime monitors and automatic change/assurance triggers.
PROPERTIES.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A safety claim is valid only while its material assumptions are evidenced; monitor the few premises whose failure can change control or acceptance.
PROPERTIES.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: An assumption spreadsheet is optional; explicit, current and actionable premise state is the property.
